title: audit: no read/view audit — "who viewed which record" is unanswerable, blocking regulated-industry deals
body:
## Summary

`sys_audit_log` covers writes only. `actionFor()` in `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts` maps exactly three events:

```ts
function actionFor(event: string): 'create' | 'update' | 'delete' | null {
  if (event === 'afterInsert') return 'create';
  if (event === 'afterUpdate') return 'update';
  if (event === 'afterDelete') return 'delete';
```

There is no read/view/export action, and the shipped audit views confirm the scope — `writes_only` filters on `['create','update','delete','restore']`, `auth_events` on `['login','logout','permission_change']`.

So the platform cannot answer **"who viewed this customer record, and when"**.

## Why this matters commercially

Found while scoping a bank CRM RFI (VTB Shanghai SME). The requirement is explicit and not unusual:

> 客户数据全部操作（含查看与导出）均记录日志 — *all operations on client data, **including views and exports**, are logged*

Every regulated-industry buyer asks this in the first security review — banking, insurance, securities, healthcare, government. Today the only honest answer on the coverage matrix is "requires customisation", which turns a standard-product checkbox into a line item on every deal in those verticals. In that project alone it was quoted at ~45 person-days of custom work.

The surrounding pieces are already strong, which makes the gap more conspicuous: the row shape is complete (actor, delegated actor, object, record id, before/after values, source IP, user agent, tenant), and retention already exceeds what finance typically asks for (90d online + 7y archive vs. the common 5y requirement).

## Design considerations

Reads vastly outnumber writes, so a naive synchronous write per read would wreck response times (the same RFI carries a 2s record-open / 1s query budget). Suggested shape:

- **Configurable scope** — per object, opt-in; not global-on.
- **Sensitivity-triggered** — ideally driven by a field/object sensitivity label rather than a hand-maintained list (see the separate data-classification discussion).
- **Async, batched writes** off the request path.
- **Sampling vs. full capture** as two modes — full for a short list of sensitive objects, sampled elsewhere.
- Decide what counts as a "view": record detail open only, or list/search results too. Banks differ on this; make it declarable rather than assumed.

## Packaging note

This looks like a natural **enterprise-tier** capability (the buyer is the compliance/internal-audit function, not the app author), and it would pair with export alerting and data classification as a coherent compliance bundle. The existing AI-governance precedent — neutral seam in the open runtime, policy in `security-enterprise` — seems like the right split here too: the audit-write seam belongs in `plugin-audit`, the policy/enforcement in the enterprise package.

## Verified against

`0f539bd` — `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts`.
